hypothesis.statement: T17's hypothesis is CONFIRMED IN KIND and much narrower than posed: an ordered transposition does hide inside the CANDIDATE set, but the ordered-sequence comparison T17 named (`run it over all 11 in one pass with fndiff.datum_relocs`) cannot see it, because 10 of the 11 have DIFFERING instruction streams and a bare index compare on those is dominated by schedule displacement -- run that way it returns 10 UNDECIDABLE and 1 BENIGN, and it also fabricates apparent transpositions out of pure reorders. What decides an ordered mismatch is the REGISTER FIELD read at the SAME POSITION: crossed registers mean each datum still reaches the same register and only the emission order moved (a schedule fact); the same register at the same position under the same mnemonic receiving a DIFFERENT datum is the transposition. NEXT LANE: the screen is UNDECIDABLE on 175 functions image-wide, almost all of them for `UNPAIRED` mismatches (304 rows) in streams whose relocation counts agree but whose words do not. An alignment (difflib over the key sequences) instead of a raw index compare would decide some of those, and is the cheapest remaining widening.

windows_tried: bare ordered index compare (T17's own formulation): 11 CANDIDATE -> 1 BENIGN, 10 UNDECIDABLE. Refuted as a decision procedure.

index compare + whole-function mirror search: 11 -> 8 DEFECT, 1 BENIGN, 2 UNDECIDABLE. + conversion-magic and same-instruction exclusions: recall on the 8 known TRANSPOSED collapsed 7/8 -> 1/8. Over-corrected.
+ the REGISTER-FIELD rule (crossed = REORDER, same-slot = DATUM-SWAP): THE SHIPPED FORM.
